summary: This House resolution supports recognizing January 9, 2026, as National Law Enforcement Appreciation Day by expressing gratitude for officers nationwide, honoring those killed or injured in duty, and urging Americans to hold ceremonies showing respect for law enforcement.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is purely symbolic and contains no provisions related to federal budgets, appropriations, or expenditures of any kind.
No tax-related language or implications appear in the bill text.
The bill does not address healthcare policy, coverage, or delivery systems.
While law enforcement is mentioned, the resolution makes no reference to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No content related to immigration, borders, or enforcement of immigration law.
The resolution contains no language concerning reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions or references to military or defense spending.
The bill does not engage with environmental regulations or climate policy.
No references to welfare programs, entitlements, or social services.
The resolution makes no mention of schools, education funding, or school choice.
No discussion of drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.

The resolution explicitly honors and expresses support for law enforcement officers and their role in upholding public safety and the rule of law. This constitutes a tangential but genuine expression of support for policing, which aligns with the +1 end of the spectrum (tougher sentencing and policing). Because the measure is purely symbolic and does not enact policy changes, the magnitude is small.
No content related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
The resolution contains no references to foreign aid or international assistance.
